question: What is the primary purpose of using teleconferencing in modern healthcare?

options.A: Connecting providers and patients across physical distances
options.B: Eliminating the need for any laboratory testing
options.C: Replacing all physical clinics with online portals
options.D: Reducing the number of working hours for midwives

explanation: Teleconferencing uses technology primarily to bridge the gap between people who are far apart. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T4#BMP123_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why is teleconferencing particularly useful for maternal care in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: It completely stops the occurrence of postpartum bleeding
options.B: It allows quick specialist consults without difficult travel
options.C: It provides free electricity to rural health centres
options.D: It removes the need for village health education

explanation: Rural patients often face long, difficult journeys to reach specialists, which virtual consults help bypass. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T4#BMP123_U4_T4_h1)

question: Who typically manages the settings and entry of participants in a virtual meeting room?
explanation: The host holds administrative control to manage attendees and meeting settings. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T4#BMP123_U4_T4_h2)

question: Which of the following features is most useful when a midwife needs to show an ultrasound scan to a remote doctor?
explanation: Screen sharing allows the remote doctor to clearly view the image displayed on the midwife's device. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T4#BMP123_U4_T4_h2)

question: A midwife at a primary health centre wants to check on a breastfeeding mother who was discharged yesterday without making a physical home visit. What is the best digital approach?

options.A: Send a printed pamphlet through the mail system
options.B: Cancel all follow-up care until complications arise
options.C: Conduct a video call to observe latching and maternal recovery
options.D: Wait until the child turns one year old for a check

explanation: A video call allows visual assessment of feeding and healing without requiring travel. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T4#BMP123_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common clinical use of virtual meetings in midwifery?
explanation: Virtual meetings facilitate communication and observation, but physical surgery requires hands-on presence. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T4#BMP123_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is a major technical challenge affecting virtual healthcare delivery in many Nigerian regions?

options.A: Unstable internet and frequent power outages
options.B: Lack of available mobile phone devices
options.C: An overabundance of fiber optic cables
options.D: Excessive speed of mobile data networks

explanation: Infrastructural gaps like erratic power and weak signals remain major hurdles for digital health. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T4#BMP123_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why is having a power backup like an inverter crucial for clinical teleconferencing?

options.A: It automatically lowers the cost of monthly data subscriptions
options.B: It eliminates background noise from the clinic environment
options.C: It improves the visual resolution of the computer monitor
options.D: It prevents sudden loss of connection during active patient discussions

explanation: Power cuts can abruptly terminate a session, disrupting critical clinical communications. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T4#BMP123_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why must a midwife conduct virtual patient consultations in a private, enclosed room?

options.A: To ensure the internet signal travels faster through the walls
options.B: To maintain patient confidentiality and prevent unauthorized listening
options.C: To comply with rules regarding room temperature
options.D: To prevent the computer screen from getting dusty

explanation: Private spaces ensure that sensitive health details are not exposed to bystanders. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T4#BMP123_U4_T4_h5)

question: What security feature helps prevent uninvited guests from joining a healthcare video conference?
explanation: Passwords and waiting rooms give the host control over who enters the virtual space. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T4#BMP123_U4_T4_h5)

question: How can community health workers assist rural patients during virtual clinical sessions?

options.A: By disconnecting the internet when the signal becomes too strong
options.B: By charging extra fees for every minute spent online
options.C: By acting as intermediaries to help operate devices and explain terms
options.D: By performing complex surgical operations on behalf of doctors

explanation: Health workers bridge the digital literacy gap by guiding patients through the virtual process. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T4#BMP123_U4_T4_h6)

question: A rural clinic has poor internet bandwidth that cannot support high-definition video calls. What is the most practical alternative adjustment?

options.A: Switch to audio-only calls or low-bandwidth messaging platforms
options.B: Insist on face-to-face meetings located five hours away
options.C: Stop all communication with patients until fiber optic cables arrive
options.D: Demand that every patient purchase a satellite dish

explanation: Low-bandwidth options keep communication open when heavy video streaming fails. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T4#BMP123_U4_T4_h6)
